text: Soapys first idea was to eat a fine dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> At an expensive restaurant. <break time="0.8s" /> And then say that he had no money. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he would be handed quietly. <break time="0.8s" /> To a policeman. <break time="0.8s" /> And a judge would send him. <break time="0.8s" /> To the Island. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked into a bright café on Broadway. <break time="0.8s" /> Where rich people enjoyed. <break time="0.8s" /> The finest food and wine. <break time="0.8s" /> His face was shaved. <break time="0.8s" /> And his coat was neat. <break time="0.8s" /> But his old trousers and broken shoes. <break time="0.8s" /> Told a different story. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing those trousers and shoes. <break time="0.8s" /> The head waiter quickly turned him around. <break time="0.8s" /> And pushed him out onto the street. <break time="0.8s" /> On Sixth Avenue. <break time="0.8s" /> Soapy picked up a stone. <break time="0.8s" /> And threw it through a large shop window. <break time="0.8s" /> People came running. <break time="0.8s" /> Around the corner. <break time="0.8s" /> With a policeman leading the crowd. <break time="0.8s" /> Soapy stood still. <break time="0.8s" /> With his hands in his pockets. <break time="0.8s" /> And smiled at the policeman. <break time="0.8s" /> Waiting to be arrested. <break time="0.8s" /> The policeman asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had broken the window. <break time="0.8s" /> And Soapy said. <break time="0.8s" /> That he might have done it himself. <break time="0.8s" /> But the policeman believed. <break time="0.8s" /> That men who break windows. <break time="0.8s" /> Always run away. <break time="0.8s" /> So he ran after another man instead.
